classification.difficultyReason: Translate the corner cuts and folding into two base dimensions reduced by twice the cut size, solve their area equation and use the physical domain to identify all three box dimensions.

content.prompt: A piece of sheet metal 50 cm by 40 cm has squares cut out of each corner so that it can be bent and formed into a lidless box with a base area of $1200\text{ cm}^2$. Find the dimensions of the box.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the side length of each corner square. The box has height $x$ cm and base dimensions $(50-2x)$ cm and $(40-2x)$ cm, with $0<x<20$.
$$\begin{align*}(50-2x)(40-2x)&=1200\\4x^2-180x+2000&=1200\\4x^2-180x+800&=0\\x^2-45x+200&=0\\(x-5)(x-40)&=0\\x&=5\text{ or }40\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=40$ because it gives negative base dimensions. For $x=5$, the base dimensions are $50-2(5)=40$ cm and $40-2(5)=30$ cm. Their product is $1200\text{ cm}^2$.
The box is $40$ cm long, $30$ cm wide and $5$ cm high.

spec.mathematics: A 50 cm by 40 cm sheet loses four x by x corner squares, leaving a base of dimensions 50−2x and 40−2x and box height x.
